title: The hooks bridge's `latest` tag points at 0.0.1-rc.5, so an unpinned `dsh plugin add` is rejected as incompatible

reported.symptom: the hooks row never loaded: `dsh: startup failed: 1 required plugin did not activate`, and the service went into a restart loop (267 cycles, 2.5h down)
reported.runtime_trace: unpinned install resolved the bridge's stale `latest` tag: `latest: 0.0.1-rc.5, alpha: 0.2.1-alpha.5, next: 0.2.1-rc.2`. The reply in the thread reproduced the rejection through the plugin manager itself: `dsh: installation rejected: Plugin @deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code@0.0.1-rc.5 is incompatible with dsh 0.2.1-rc.2: ... / dsh: nothing was installed.`
user_hypotheses: the hooks plugin is missing from the runtime (it is: the missing case is only a warning, which is a different symptom)
rolling back to 0.2.0-rc.2 would recover (it does not: newer session logs are refused)
`dsh plugin allow-version` is the remedy the message suggests (it would run an incompatible legacy plugin)
reported.root_cause: 0.0.1-rc.5 requires ^0.0.1-rc.5 of dsh-llm, dsh-session, dsh-agent, dsh-tools and others, so every @deepseek-ai/dsh-* peer is unmet against the 0.2.1 runtimeline
reported.fix_verified_by_reporter: pinning @deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code@0.2.1-rc.2 installs cleanly (and the reporter keeps only a symlink inside the profile)

deviations: candidate mode: the rejection happened before any installation, and the thread's reply reproduces it verbatim through `dsh plugin --profile web add`, so there is no profile to replay

the unpinned spec → version resolution is not re-simulated; the resolved version is the tag snapshot the report records, re-checked against the registry on 2026-10-26 (latest=0.0.1-rc.5, next=0.2.1-rc.3)

the report's startup-side message names @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm as the incompatible package; the requirement key used here (@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent) is one of the peers the report enumerates verbatim (`requires ^0.0.1-rc.5 of dsh-llm, dsh-session, dsh-agent, dsh-tools and others`), and every one of them is unmet for the same reason
the second half of the report (row present but unimportable stays silent, row present but incompatible is fatal) is not modelled: import-level attribution is T-102
session-log downgrade refusal and the duplicate-resolution `already registered` conflict are out of scope for admission
